sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (national unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax regimes)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition, with EU-derived commercial legislation)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies), as subsequently amended; Articles 710-1 through 710-26 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée regime), Article 179 (publication in the RESA and legal personality), and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 11 November 2015 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); e-filing portal: lodge.lbr.lu; registry office: 8-10, rue Henri M. Schnadt, L-2530 Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarial deed of incorporation) with annexed statuts (articles of association), submitted electronically by the notary via the coordinated RCS filing form (Formulaire B / e-BR).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for the SARL is EUR 12,000 under Article 710-1(2) of the amended Law of 10 August 1915. Capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation in cash or in kind. Cash contributions must be blocked on a company-in-formation account opened with a Luxembourg credit institution, and the notary must obtain the bank's blocked-funds certificate. In-kind contributions must be valued in a report of an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé). Transfers of shares to non-shareholders require consent of shareholders holding at least three-quarters of the capital, subject to any stricter clause in the statutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
The undersigned, holding the entire share capital of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée [Company], acting as the general meeting, resolve:

FIRST: The deed of incorporation and the articles of association executed before [Notary] on [Date] are ratified in full. Each founding shareholder's subscription, aggregating EUR 12,000 of paid-up capital, is approved and the blocked-funds certificate acknowledged.

SECOND: The registered office is fixed at [Street Address], L-[Postcode] [City], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

THIRD: [Name] is appointed gérant of the Company for [term], with authority to exercise all powers within the corporate purpose and to represent the Company towards third parties.

FOURTH: The gérant is authorized to complete all statutory registrations and formalities.

Adopted unanimously on [Date].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; all procedures accessible via MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon notarial incorporation, the notary files the SARL with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL), obtaining the corporate matricule (national identification number which serves as the corporate TIN). For VAT, file registration form 640 with the AEDT before commencing taxable activity; the VAT number is issued in the format LU + 8 digits. A non-established foreign supplier of digital services may register directly for VAT under form 640 without an RCSL establishment, or alternatively make use of the OSS mechanism in its EU member state of establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is a capital company fully taxable on Luxembourg-source taxable income, subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune); pass-through treatment is not available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Qualifying Luxembourg groups may elect fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) for corporate income and municipal business tax purposes for a minimum five-year period. Participation exemption applies to qualifying dividends and capital gains. Hybrid mismatch limitations under ATAD apply and no elective hybrid entity classification is available under Luxembourg domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) implemented under the Luxembourg VAT Law and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for domestic small-business franchise exemption; mandatory VAT registration required above EUR 35,000. Non-resident suppliers of digital services to Luxembourg non-taxable persons have no threshold and are registrable from the first euro unless using the EU OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control regime exists for standard B2B VAT invoices. Invoices must comply with EU VAT Directive Articles 226–236 and be issued within one month of supply. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies only to public procurement contracts via the PEPPOL/EN 16931 network. Future obligations may arise from the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT where the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days and the supplier retains adequate transport and customs evidence. Cross-border services to non-EU customers are generally outside Luxembourg VAT scope where place-of-supply rules seat the supply outside the EU; B2B services to EU business customers are reverse-charged, and B2C digital services are taxed at the customer's location. Digital cross-border subscription revenue therefore does not ordinarily rely on Luxembourg zero-rating but on place-of-supply and outside-scope treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU or electronic AES export declaration)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer receipt evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Proof of arrival or customs clearance in the destination country (recommended supplementary evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to documentary audit by the AEDT. Failure to substantiate export status triggers VAT reassessment at 17%, default interest, administrative fines up to 100% of the evaded tax, and, in cases of deliberate fraud, criminal prosecution of directors. Any VAT refund already paid may be clawed back together with interest, and directors or persons knowingly participating in a false zero-rating claim may incur joint liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision, payment systems, and AML/CFT enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility exists for both capital and current account transactions under EU Treaty provisions (Articles 63-65 TFEU). No exchange control approvals are required for inbound investment, profit remittance, or dividend distribution. Cross-border payments and financial transactions above EUR 12,500 are subject to BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting. A 15% domestic dividend withholding tax applies unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty; the Luxembourg participation exemption and treasury simplification may apply. For micro-SaaS subscription revenue, the receipts qualify as current-account services income, which is freely remittable without central bank consent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion deadlines, and no requirement to maintain a minimum share of foreign currency receipts. Export earnings may be retained in original currency or converted at the holder's discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (also usable as Capital Escrow Account)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Fintech EMI solutions (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business) can accept merchant payouts from Paddle and Lemon Squeezy under an EEA e-money licence or passporting regime. However, the SARL must maintain a full Luxembourg credit institution or licensed EMI account for statutory capital, payroll, direct tax, and social security obligations. EMIs are generally not suitable as the sole treasury rail for a Luxembourg tax-resident company due to possible restrictions on physical bank references and a higher chance of account freeze in low-volume cross-border SaaS trades.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No physical attendance is mandated for SARL bank account opening. Lux-embourg banks generally accept remote video KYC with notarized corporate extracts, director passport copies, and standard beneficial-ownership declarations when the AML risk tier is low. A physical or in-person video interview may still be requested for ultimate shareholders based in high-risk jurisdictions, or if the corporate structure includes complex intermediaries. For a single-purpose consumer micro-SaaS SARL settled in Luxembourg with identifiable EU founders, remote onboarding is a viable standard route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Contradictory or artificial subscription revenue flow from overseas merchant acquirers (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy) without clear commercial explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited subscription revenue ledger, SaaS platform dashboard export, PCI-DSS compliance attestation, signed end-user licence agreement (EULA), merchant of record agreement, and annual financial projection; explain payout waterfall from merchant to SARL bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder or manager tax residence in a non-EU high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., sanctioned country or FATF blacklisted entity).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML-resilient proof of source of wealth/funds, notarized identity and residence certificates, clean criminal records, bank reference from cleared FI, beneficial ownership register extract (RBE), and a professional legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital deposit of EUR 12,000 minimum received from an opaque third-party without documented shareholder remittance trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution resolution of the shareholders, bank SWIFT MT103 plus correspondent trail, signed subscription agreement, notarized initial notarial deed, bank reference letter of the remitting shareholder, and source-of-funds evidence (salary slips, asset sale contract, or corporate liquidation statement).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid disbursement pattern from few foreign low-tier corporate merchants to Luxembourg account without payroll or tax history; SARL flagged as a front for payment laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete merchant contract and payout terms with Paddle/Lemon Squeezy, customer subscription records, database access for nexus reporting, tax filings (CT1/VAT), employment contracts and payroll register, movement declarations of trade receivables, and internal treasury/funding policy for liquidity needs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Luxembourg SARL, shareholder equity or convertible loan capital should be remitted via SWIFT MT103/MT202 using a BCL-recognised bank reference. Payment purpose field must state 'Share capital contribution / participation - SARL incorporation' or 'Subordinated shareholder loan - investment'. The company must retain a notarised share subscription spreadsheet and statutory accounts. For statistical reporting, use BCL balance-of-payments category D1 (direct investment) — 'Equity capital' or 'Intercompany debt (loan)' — whichever applies. Verification in Luxembourg: shareholder bank statement, SWIFT confirmation, and the notarial deed establishing the SARL. For loan injections, an arm's-length loan agreement and CSSF-compliant interest rate terms are required to avoid thin capitalisation recategorisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound supplier and operational payments rely on SEPA Credit Transfers (EUR) within the EEA, and SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR or third-currency settlement. For Paddle and Lemon Squeezy trade settlements, the standard rail is SWIFT/SEPA payout from the merchant of record to the SARL's Luxembourg bank, usually in EUR. Commercial letters of credit (documentary L/C) are not relevant for micro-SaaS subscription revenue; they only apply to physical goods trade. For recurring outbound licence/reseller payments, MT103 with purpose code 'Software subscription fees' or 'Royalties & licence fees' should be used, accompanied by an invoice and underlying contract in the bank's export-control review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (plain vanilla) offered by an EEA-licensed credit institution under a standard ISDA master agreement
Cross-currency swaps (buy EUR/sell USD) for financing or coupon flows, subject to bank credit lines and CSSF prudential oversight
EUR/USD or EUR/GBP options on regulated markets (less necessary for a micro-SaaS model)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not prohibited but are generally unnecessary and operationally unavailable because EUR is a freely convertible currency; their use requires explicit counterparty credit approval and specific justification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (comptes annuels) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 8 months after financial year-end; shareholder approval within 6 months; deposit with RCS within 1 month after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS default notice, court-ordered compliance under penalty (astreinte), civil fines, and repeated non-compliance may result in administrative strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayer: due by 31 December of the year following the tax year; extension only if expressly granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax, and estimated assessment by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 December of the year following the tax year; net wealth tax position assessed as of 1 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest, late-filing penalty up to 10%, and estimated assessment if the return is not filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December; updated declaration must be filed within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines in Luxembourg RBE exposure of up to EUR 125,000 and public disclosure of continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is required if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average employees above 50. A micro SaaS entity below these thresholds is exempt from mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounting; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts and may be applied voluntarily to individual accounts under certain conditions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On any share transfer, the transfer must be minuted, the register of members updated, and the RBE declaration updated within 30 days. The annual RBE confirmation, due by 31 December, certifies that the current beneficial ownership data remain accurate and does not suspend the separate 30-day update duty triggered by share transfers.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT + municipal business tax ~6.75% in Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for eligible investments), notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity, and participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 200 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via the eCDF (Electronic Corporate Tax Filing) portal of the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; extensions up to 31 December may be granted upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income if tax resident; for non-resident, only Luxembourg-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions (e.g., IP box exemption, NID, tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions directly attributable to Luxembourg-source income.
Utilize prior-year losses subject to continuity of business and ownership tests.
For non-residents, only Luxembourg permanent establishment income is subject to municipal tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits (e.g., on dividends received)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief or EU directives if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €250 to €2,500 per month, plus 0.6% interest per month on unpaid tax. Willful omission may lead to criminal penalties and fines up to €25,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 12 months; treaty rates often 5% or 0% for substantial shareholdings)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the source country, complete Form 22 (for reduced WHT) or Form 23 (for exemption), and provide evidence of beneficial ownership. The Luxembourg tax authority issues a 'Quittance' or 'Attestation' for treaty purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if qualifying; treaty rates often 0-10%). Interest: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Directive; treaty rates often 0-10%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group turnover (Master File and Local File required); CbC report for groups with consolidated revenue > EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in IP, financing, and holding activities. For a micro SaaS company, substance is evidenced by local management, employees, and operational decision-making. Failure to demonstrate substance may lead to reclassification as a shell company and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of revenue, false deductions, or failure to file returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; additional tax penalties of 10% to 200% of evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and potential imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No physical presence, no employees, no real business activity, or passive income without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 15% WHT on deemed distributions; fines up to €100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for taxes due if they fail to ensure substance; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, or maintaining inadequate records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for entities; imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; license revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; civil liability for damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of the adjustment, and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing.
